discovery: Prediction and discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: moiré quantum materials and strongly correlated electrons
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by about 1.1 degrees form nearly flat electronic bands, a 'magic angle' where kinetic energy is quenched and interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero realized this device and discovered correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, with a phase diagram reminiscent of the cuprates, in a material made of carbon alone. This theory-experiment loop created the field of twistronics: the twist angle became a new tuning knob that turns ordinary layered crystals into designable quantum materials. It opened a new frontier that laboratories worldwide have confirmed and extended, including our own atomic-scale imaging of flat-band correlations. Moiré systems have since produced orbital ferromagnetism, correlated Chern insulators, Wigner crystals and, recently, the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect. Few discoveries in the past decade have reshaped condensed matter physics so broadly.
